questions.stem: When an enzyme is heated above its optimum temperature, it loses its function. Which level of protein structure is most directly disrupted?

options.text: Primary structure -- the peptide bonds break
Tertiary structure -- the 3D shape is altered as weak bonds break (denaturation)
The protein is converted into a carbohydrate

questions.explanation: High temperatures break the weak bonds (hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, disulfide bridges) that maintain the tertiary (3D) structure of the protein. This changes the shape of the active site, so substrates can no longer fit -- the enzyme is denatured. The primary structure (amino acid sequence) remains intact.

questions.stem: Sickle cell anaemia is caused by a single amino acid change in the haemoglobin protein. This demonstrates the importance of which level of protein structure?

options.text: Primary structure, because changing one amino acid alters the entire 3D shape and function
The lipid content of the protein

questions.explanation: The primary structure (amino acid sequence) determines all higher levels of protein structure. In sickle cell anaemia, a single amino acid substitution (glutamic acid to valine) changes the protein's properties, causing haemoglobin molecules to stick together and red blood cells to become sickle-shaped. This shows that even one amino acid change can have dramatic effects.

questions.stem: Collagen is a structural protein made of three polypeptide chains wound around each other. This arrangement describes which level of protein structure?
questions.explanation: Quaternary structure refers to the arrangement of multiple polypeptide chains (subunits) within a protein. Collagen's three polypeptide chains forming a triple helix is an example of quaternary structure. Haemoglobin (four subunits) is another example. Not all proteins have quaternary structure -- only those with more than one polypeptide chain.

questions.stem: A scientist uses a chemical that breaks disulfide bridges in a protein. How would this affect the protein?

options.text: The amino acid sequence would change
The protein would lose its specific 3D shape and likely lose its function
The protein would become more active
The protein would break into individual amino acids

questions.explanation: Disulfide bridges (formed between cysteine amino acids) are strong bonds that help maintain the tertiary structure (3D shape) of proteins. Breaking these bonds would cause the protein to unfold, losing its specific shape and therefore its function. The primary structure would remain intact, but the functional shape would be lost.

questions.stem: Alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets are examples of which level of protein structure, and what type of bond maintains them?
questions.explanation: Alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets are the two main types of secondary structure, formed by regular folding patterns in the polypeptide chain. They are held in place by hydrogen bonds between the C=O and N-H groups of the peptide backbone. These structures contribute to the overall 3D shape of the protein.
